claim_text: People who eat little or no oily fish may have lower dietary EPA/DHA intake, but the need for supplementation depends on overall diet, fortified foods, product composition and individual context; low fish intake alone is not a diagnosis or universal indication.
health_goal_or_outcome: Support evidence-based nutrient assessment and avoid automatic supplementation.

population.other_context: People with low oily-fish intake considering omega-3 products.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Food and/or supplemental sources; verify exact formulation and label.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Omega-3 fact sheet describes food sources including fish and algal oils.
limitations: No universal dose; distinguish EPA and DHA amounts and consider medicines and clinical context.
Exact source passages and clinical applicability require full appraisal.
